title: Yusuf and the joint festival (paraphrase)
topic: After a wave of migration a parish and a mosque organise a shared festival: the priest welcomes Yusuf, the parish opens its hall, the mosque women cook, the choir sings, the children play, the mayor thanks both communities
tail_E: Before dinner, Yusuf and the priest say a brief
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'prayer' is the natural continuation of 'Yusuf and the priest say a brief' at a joint festival of a mosque and a parish; the word and its German equivalents (Gebet / beten) occur nowhere in the units or the tail, and no form of 'pray' is used. ' prayer' is a single Pythia token (id 15851); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.71, next candidate 'sermon' ~ 0.04).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F16B, parish and mosque, Yusuf, paraphrase)
notes: Formulation B, domain religion: independent re-phrasing of the ten meaning units of F16A in both languages (same events, same order, same name Yusuf). The priest is 'the parish priest' / 'der Gemeindepfarrer', the parish 'the church community' / 'die Kirchengemeinde', the songs 'hymns' / 'Choräle', the speech 'a brief address' / 'eine kurze Ansprache'; unit 9 uses the reflexive 'sich bedanken bei' (non-separable). Unit 5 uses inseparable 'überlässt' (makes its hall available; 'verleihen' is unusual for rooms, and 'stellt ... zur Verfügung' would close the verb bracket before the adjunct, which the C2 switch must keep open). Unit 6 uses non-separable 'bereiten' (not 'zubereiten'). No separable verbs. Subjects vary between the protagonist, other people, institutions and the celebration itself. Unit 9 reads naturally in German, units 1 and 10 in English.
